classification.difficultyReason: Counts single and compound card events, distinguishing inclusive or, intersection and mutually exclusive categories.

content.prompt: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of playing cards. Find the probability that the card chosen:

answer.worked:
There are 13 Hearts in the 52-card pack.

$$P(\text{Heart})=\frac{13}{52}=\frac{1}{4}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: is a court card (that is, a King, Queen or Jack)

answer.worked:
Each of the four suits has three court cards, giving $4\times3=12$ court cards.

$$P(\text{court card})=\frac{12}{52}=\frac{3}{13}.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: has a face value between 2 and 8 inclusive

answer.worked:
The seven values $2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ each occur in four suits, giving $7\times4=28$ cards.

$$P(2\text{ to }8)=\frac{28}{52}=\frac{7}{13}.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: is a Heart or a court card

answer.worked:
The favourable cards are the 13 Hearts and the nine court cards in the other three suits. This counts the three Heart court cards only once.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Heart or court card})&=\frac{13+9}{52}\\P(\text{Heart or court card})&=\frac{22}{52}\\P(\text{Heart or court card})&=\frac{11}{26}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: is a Heart and a court card

answer.worked:
The favourable cards are the King, Queen and Jack of Hearts.

$$P(\text{Heart and court card})=\frac{3}{52}.$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: has a face value between 2 and 8 inclusive and is a court card

answer.worked:
No King, Queen or Jack has a face value from 2 to 8 inclusive, so there are no favourable cards.

$$P(2\text{ to }8\text{ and court card})=\frac{0}{52}=0.$$

children.label: g
children.prompt: has a face value between 2 and 8 inclusive or is a court card

answer.worked:
There are 28 cards with values from 2 to 8 and 12 court cards. These groups have no cards in common.

$$\begin{align*}P(2\text{ to }8\text{ or court card})&=\frac{28+12}{52}\\P(2\text{ to }8\text{ or court card})&=\frac{40}{52}\\P(2\text{ to }8\text{ or court card})&=\frac{10}{13}.\end{align*}$$
